the extraction of jet transport parameter in heavy-ion collisions.
a quantitative extraction of the jet quenching parameter q ˆ from combined data at the Relativistic Heavy Ion Collider (RHIC) and Large Hadron Collider (LHC).

the quantitative extraction of the jet quenching parameter q ˆ, which is a measure of the jet energy loss, by comparing the theoretical calculations to the experimental data on suppression of hadron spectra at RHIC and the LHC.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the jet transport parameter is quantitatively extracted with a precision of about 30% from combined RHIC and Lhc data on single inclusive hadron production.

the jet transport parameter extracted from the combined data on single inclusive hadron suppression at RHIC and the LHC is q ˆ = 1.6 ± 0.4 GeV 2 fm, with the initial time τ ₀ = 0.4 fm / c for the quark jet with the initial energy E = 10 GeV / c.
the jet transport parameter is q ˆ = 1.5 ± 0.4 GeV 2 fm at RHIC and q ˆ =2.2 ± 1.0 GeV 2 at the LHC.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the jet transport parameter is found to be q ˆ ∼ 1.2 GeV 2 fm in the center-of-mass energy range of s = 200 - 2.76 TeV, which is in good agreement with the theoretical prediction from the perturbative QCD based Langevin model.

the extracted values of q ˜ for both RHIC and the LHC are consistent with each other and with the theoretical estimates from the lattice calculations, but are still larger than what the pQCD based calculations predict.
the jet transport parameter is not a constant but is a function of temperature and energy of the jet.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the extracted jet transport parameter q ˆ is independent of the initial time, initial jet energy, jet energy fraction lost to the medium, jet quenching model used, the number of spatial dimensions in the hydrodynamic model, and whether the hydrodynamic model is ( 2 +1 ) D or a full ( 3 +1 ) D model, as long as the hydrodynamic model and the jet quenching are consistently implemented.
the extracted values for q ˆ at RHIC and the LHC are consistent with each other within errors.
the combined RHIC and Lhc jet quenching data is consistent with a universal q ˆ value, independent of the initial energy of the parton, and independent of the collision energy.
